research.title: Robustness of Intent Classification to Conversational Noise
bullets: Designed supervised evaluation protocols with supervisor guidance to isolate effects of spelling variation, filler phrases, and paraphrasing on intent classification.
Compared classifier behavior across clean and perturbed utterances, examining confusion patterns and documenting ambiguities introduced by meaning-altering perturbations.

research.title: Cross-Domain Generalization in Negation-Aware Sentiment Classification
bullets: Designed cross-domain sentiment experiments with supervisor guidance, separating domain vocabulary effects from negation handling through controlled training and evaluation splits.
Evaluated lexical and neural baselines using macro-averaged metrics, then categorized errors involving negation scope, mixed sentiment, and domain-specific expressions.

publications.title: Negation Sensitivity in Cross-Domain Sentiment Classification: A Controlled Baseline Comparison

projects.title: Comparative Evaluation of Extractive Summarization Methods
bullets: Implemented sentence ranking using term frequency weighting and graph centrality, applying consistent tokenization and summary length constraints across methods.
Compared generated summaries against reference summaries using lexical overlap measures and manually inspected redundancy, missing context, and sentence ordering.

projects.title: Sequence Labeling for Named Entity Recognition
bullets: Implemented token classification and recurrent sequence labeling baselines with shared preprocessing, padding masks, and label mappings for named entity recognition.
Compared entity-level precision and recall across models, inspecting boundary mistakes, unseen entity mentions, and errors associated with infrequent labels.

projects.title: Sparse and Dense Retrieval for Question Matching
bullets: Implemented lexical retrieval and pooled neural representation baselines to rank candidate questions, maintaining identical candidate collections and query preprocessing.
Compared ranking quality using reciprocal rank and recall measures, examining failures involving paraphrases, rare terminology, and superficially similar questions.
